To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) change blindness is induced when the initial preview of a scene is brief and when the interruption is brief and contains only a small number of elements, and (2) change blindness is eliminated when the initial preview is long, when the interruption is long and contains a large number of elements, or when the interruption is replaced by a blank field.
change blindness is a failure of perception, and that it occurs when attentional resources are diverted from a scene during an interruption.

(a) change blindness can be induced by brief blank fields placed between alternating displays; (b) this change blindness is not due to the blank field itself; (c) the change blindness is due to the failure to maintain a representation of the original display across the interruption; and (d) the representation of the original is lost because it is not stabilized by focused attention.
